stories.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after Trump personally intervenes, a week after his ouster
stories.summary:
Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, a little more than a week after he resigned amid allegations of multiple affairs, including one with a woman US intelligence links to a Chinese spy plot.

- The board had rejected calls for Huang's return until President Trump called it. Its statement says the decision came with "input from senior levels of the United States government," and Trump has publicly taken credit on CNBC
- The NYT says the woman is a recruit of China's Ministry of State Security and a top executive at a Singapore AI cloud firm accused of illegally selling Nvidia chips to China. The relationship reportedly helped route $7.5B in Nvidia AI chips to Chinese firms
- WIRED's sources said the board's main problem was Huang's "lack of candor," amid allegations of multiple affairs, including one with a direct report
- CFO Colette Kress served as interim CEO in the meantime, promising across-the-board pay raises and more equity
- Huang agreed to testify before Congress, and Democrats have opened a second investigation into Nvidia's China sales and what they call Huang's "scheme" with Trump
- Nvidia stock slid on the scandal, and investors proposed a class action

- Google had threatened that schools dropping its AI would lose Search too, since AI Overviews are built into Search. It later tried to walk that policy back
- Google's own employees have joined the criticism: the Alphabet Workers Union objected to Google requiring its AI tools be bundled with Search
- Parents and educators worry that easy, machine-generated answers are leaving kids less capable
- NYC mayor Zohran Mamdani and former FTC chair Lina Khan accused Google of acting as an unregulated monopoly
- DuckDuckGo has been courting frustrated schools with its search engine and options to disable AI features

stories.title: Hugging Face introduces harness adapters to tune models to specific agent harnesses
stories.summary: Hugging Face announced "harness adapters," a way to adapt a chosen model to the agent harness it runs in, pitched as improving both performance and cost. The source item carries only the title, so details on how the adapters are trained, which models and harnesses are supported, and benchmark gains aren't available yet.

sources.title: Introducing harness adapters: adapt your favorite model to your harness to improve performance and cost
